newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money rates crash on improved liquidity.
newsitem.headline: India call money rates crash on improved liquidity.

text.p: Indian call money rates fell sharply on unexpected improvement in liquidity to end Tuesday in the 2.75-3.25 percent range against the day's opening 9.0-9.5 percent, dealers said.
The surge in liquidity came as a surprise to most dealers who had expected call money rates to remain firm today ahead of a securities auction.
The Reserve Bank of India auctions 20 billion rupees of five-year government of India securities later on Tuesday.
"We are still not clear at the end of the day why call money rates fell today," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"Several banks were caught unawares....Quite a few deals took place between nine and ten percent."
One dealer said interest payments on government securities on Saturday could be one reason for the fall in rates.
"Around nine billion rupees have been paid to banks by way of interest," he said. "This eased liquidity considerably."
Another dealer said funds withdrawn for local festivals earlier in the month were now flowing back to banks.
Dealers said prices of government securities moved up slightly in sluggish trade.

"The market continues to be wary...no-one is prepared to lock up funds now," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "With call money rates gyrating wildly, we cannot take positions with any degree of certainty.
The 13.50 percent 1997 governemnt of India stock traded on Tuesday at 102.56 rupees against its latest price of 102.39, dealers said.
The treasury bill maturing in February traded at yields between 9.25 and 9.40 percent against last traded yields of 9.49 percent, they said.
Dealers said there were no trades in certificates of deposit and commercial paper on Tuesday.
